original.description: ANUBIS (Asteroid NUdging By Ion-beam Shepherding) is a potential future Planetary Defence Cornerstone aiming to demonstrate the "ion beam shepherd" concept, which makes use of ion thrusters to deflect asteroids. The concept is of great interest to Planetary Defence and the scientific community, as demonstrated by various assessments, and in particular highlighted by the UN Space Mission Planning Advisory Group (SMPAG). The concept is one of the most promising candidates for deflecting potentially hazardous asteroids, when there is time enough to apply this technology.

original.description: The objective of the activity is to define and develop a free space optical communication testbed suitable for testing a cross-atmospheric optical connectivity in the horizontal link between Tallinn and Helsinki. Targeted Improvements: To create a terrestrial testbed capability allowing for demonstration and long-term communication testing. The testbed will provide information on the long-distance atmospheric channel and the stability of the optical links in fixed and mobile configuration. The testbed facility will support new technology developments for optical and quantum satellite communication. Description: Most of satellite constellations developed these days include intersatellite links. However, the adaptation of cross-atmospheric links remains to be progressing slowly. One of the challenges is the limited availability of outdoor, free-space testbeds. The proposed testbed facility will enable testing over the long-distance, cross-atmospheric channel created between two stations located in Tallinn and Helsinki. The testbed will allow for fixed-points free-space optical connection, demonstrating and validating a continuous datalink between interoperable terminals and transceivers aligned with satellite optical communication standards. The testbed should allow to collect and analyse information on the atmospheric channel over multiple seasons. It should monitor weather conditions and investigate beam dissipation dynamics and various mitigation strategies. The spatially dynamic optical links will also be demonstrated to test and validate a free-space optical datalink between moving terminals. The testbed should foresee and facilitate testing of quantum-encrypted free-space optical communication capabilities. The preparation to demonstrate data-relay with a satellite link is planned to be included in the activity.

original.description: The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) safeguards system is designed to verify States' legal undertakings to use nuclear material for exclusively peaceful purposes. States declare their nuclear material and activities to the IAEA, and the IAEA verifies thecorrectness and completeness of these declarations.This requires robust and resilient GNSS trackers which can withstand sophisticated attacks (jamming, spoofing, and especially treacherous meaconing) and tampering attempts by State-level actors, providing Assured PNT (Trusted positioning data).The GNSS tracker shall be battery powered and capable of unsupervised operations. In previous projects (in particular, EL1-077) building blocks for this technology have been developed. The IAEA has expressed interest in a joint project to increase the protection against additional attacks identified and to raise the TRL level and to make the tracker ready forcommercialization. The objective of the activity is to study, design, implement and demonstrate a resilient and robust GNSS tracker to support IAEA safeguards activities, and other similar activities requiring Assured PNTThe tasks to be performed shall include:Based on EL1-077, the activity will study, design, implement and demonstrate the technologies required for the GNSS tracker, capable of detecting and mitigating jamming, meaconing and spoofing attacks, with focus on concrete uses cases and attack scenarios identified by IAEA.Additional technologies (for example tightly coupled INS and CRPAs) will be integrated into a functional prototype. original.description: Objective: To develop a proof-of-concept of a modular robust waveform for E2E communications that offers further protection for the missions, in a modular approach in accordance with the mission security needs.Description:Intentional RF interference is a threat to space missions, as it can disrupt the radio links between satellite and ground/users. There are waveform techniques that can counter or mitigate the impact of that interference but they need to be designed specifically against reference threats. This activity is aimed at developing a modular robust waveform for end-to-end (E2E) communications offering further protection for the missions, by designing the waveform aspects as well as the receiver operations. It will consider typical RF threats and tune the waveform against the most common ones, so that space missions do not have to develop new solutions for their case. The design of the modular robust waveform can include cryptographically robust spread sequences that can be used to drive a frequency hopping scheme, or a direct Sequence spread spectrum modulation, coupled with Adaptive Coding and Modulation (ACM). The adaptation algorithm of the ACM can cover both the typical Modulation and Coding schemes as well as the Transmission Security (TRANSEC) functions (e.g. Direct Sequence Spread Spectrum and Frequency Hopping), providing flexible level of protection based on the link conditions. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Consolidation of the most common RF interference signals and attacks method - Investigation of state of theart signal techniques to counter RF interference and development of a SWAT analysis to select the optimum measures for the consolidated attacks options. - Detailed design of the waveform blocks to counter the identified common RF interference threats. Particular emphasis shall be devoted to the Add-on modularity so that each block can be added as plug-in. - Development of a Proof of Concept simulator including signal generator/receiver of the waveform and assessment of the E2E performance of the proposed Waveform. - Investigation of the regulatory constraints from the Radio Frequency Compatibility with specific focus on the impact of wideband signals on ITU frequency bands allocation. The software shall be delivered under an ESA Software Community License, so that any individuals or entities within ESA Member States can access to it and can provide update to the community of users.Deliverables: Report, Software

original.description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop bundle protocol and network stack, enabling automatic high-volume end-to-enddata distribution within integratedRF and optical networks. The testbed shall be developed to test networks feature heterogenous links, e.g. in terms of data rates or latencies, and includeend users, mission and payload control centres, optical and RF ground stations and space data relay systems.TargetedImprovements:Standardised data distribution irrespective of RF or optical communication.Reduced ground segment complexity (single system for RF and optical).Automatic network-based distribution.Increased E2E data delivery accountability leveraging unified reporting.Description: The need for hybrid (optical and RF) networks is due to the volumeof data transferred by satellites 00that is ever increasing. Optical communicationpotentially combined or augmented with RF communication at higher frequencies is supporting high or very high data rates. The distribution of this datais non-trivial and faces several challenges like non-permanent connectivity and asymmetric data rates in space and on ground just to name a few. It ishighly desirable to take a reliable and interoperable end-to-end approach with a common addressing scheme to cross organisational boundaries whilebeing able to monitor and manage the overall process of data distribution.The activity will develop an integrated optical andRF scalable high-volume data distribution testbed (demonstrating beyond 1 TB per downlink) based onDisruption Tolerant Networking (DTN). The activity will develop combined software and hardware. The testbed will be tested for high speed DTN nodesconnected over Wide Area Networks, emulating end users, control centres, and ground stations connecting with simulated spacecraft. It will includemonitoring and control aspects of individual nodes and DTN Network Management. The activity will allow the gathering of valuable experience in arepresentative environment and will address the problem of reliable and efficient data distribution in heterogenous ground networks and prepares theexpected deployment of DTN in space nodes in the future.
